**Allowed origins** are set by the `origin` function passed to `cors({...})` in `worker/src/index.ts`, around lines 19–31. It applies to all routes via `app.use('*', ...)`. It echoes the request's `Origin` back if it is one of these:

- `http://localhost:4200`, an exact match (the Angular dev server).
- Any origin ending in `.pages.dev` (Cloudflare Pages, any subdomain depth).
- Any origin ending in `.workers.dev`.

A request with no `Origin` header, or with any other origin, gets `null`, so no CORS headers are sent. The allowed methods are `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` and `OPTIONS`.

**To add a custom domain**, edit that same function. Add another condition to the `if` block, for example `origin === 'https://play.example.com'`, alongside the `localhost:4200` check. Use an exact full-origin match, including the scheme and with no trailing slash. Don't use `endsWith` for a domain you own, because `evil-example.com` would match it. Don't put the domain in an array. Hono compares array entries as exact strings, which is why the code uses a function. This is also noted in `docs/code/worker/src/index.md` and `DEPLOYMENT_NOTES §4`.

No change to `wrangler.toml` is needed for CORS. After editing, redeploy the Worker. If you want the docs to stay accurate, update the CORS line in `docs/code/worker/src/index.md` too.

I didn't check the frontend's API base URL setting. If the new domain hosts the frontend, that setting must point at the Worker. That is separate from CORS.
